seo.title: Google Maps Dining Trends: Lessons for Restaurants
seo.meta_description: Google Maps' Fan-Favorite Dining List shows matcha, froyo and ube trending. What these Google Maps dining trends mean for Anaheim and Orange County restaurants.

h1: Google Maps Dining Trends: What the Fan-Favorite Dining List Teaches Orange County Restaurants
answer: Google Maps' first Fan-Favorite Dining List, from October 8, 2026, used reviews, ratings and direction searches to find Google Maps dining trends in 10 cities: matcha grew in nearly all of them, froyo mentions in New York rose 320% and ube rose 75% in Melbourne. For Anaheim and Orange County restaurants, it shows how reviews and menus shape discovery.
key_takeaways: Google analyzed reviews, ratings and direction searches.
The list covers 10 cities, none in Orange County.
Matcha grew double digits in nearly all 10 cities.
Review mentions of froyo in New York rose 320%.
Specific dishes in reviews and menus drive discovery.

sections.heading: What Google published
sections.body_html: On October 8, 2026, Google Maps released its first Fan-Favorite Dining List. Google says it used Maps reviews, ratings and aggregated searches for directions to find dining trends across 10 cities: Atlanta, Chicago, London, Melbourne, Montréal, New York, San Francisco, Santiago, Seattle and Tokyo.

sections.heading: Not Orange County data
sections.body_html: None of the 10 cities is in Orange County, so these numbers don't describe local diners. What they do show is how Google Maps reads reviews and searches to spot trends, which applies to every restaurant on Maps.

sections.heading: Trend 1: classic treats came back
sections.body_html: Google says reviews mentioning froyo in New York rose 320% year over year, cinnamon buns in Montréal rose 84% and mochi in Tokyo rose 168%, which Google links to record tourism.

sections.heading: Trend 2: matcha and earthy flavors
sections.body_html: Google says matcha grew by double digits year over year in nearly all 10 cities, including 82% in Chicago and 84% in Santiago, and by over 50% in Seattle, San Francisco, New York and Atlanta. Hojicha mentions rose 114% in London and ube 75% in Melbourne.

sections.heading: Trend 3: crispy and golden comfort food
sections.body_html: Google reports review mentions of beef tallow up 82% in Chicago, dosas up 136% in Seattle and beignets up 77% in Atlanta.

sections.heading: Beyond trends
sections.body_html: The list also names the most-navigated-to dining spot in each city, such as La Taqueria in San Francisco and Katz's Delicatessen in New York, and top-reviewed spots for big portions and small checks.

sections.heading: What this shows about Maps
sections.body_html: Google built the list from what people write in reviews and where they ask for directions. Specific dish names in reviews are visible signals. When diners mention your matcha latte, ube dessert or birria tacos by name, that detail is part of how Maps understands what you're known for.

sections.heading: What Orange County restaurants can do
sections.body_html:
1. Publish your menu as text on your website and Business Profile, with dish names people search for.
  2. Ask happy customers to mention the dish they loved in their review.
  3. Add photos of signature dishes to your profile.
  4. Reply to reviews and mention the dish when it fits naturally.
  5. Highlight seasonal or trending items you genuinely serve.

sections.heading: Don't chase every trend
sections.body_html: Adding matcha or ube to a menu only makes sense if it fits your kitchen and customers. The lesson is to make what you already do well visible, not to copy another city's trend.

sections.heading: A worked example
sections.body_html: Imagine a cafe in Garden Grove known for its pandan and ube pastries. Its menu exists only as a photo, and reviews just say great place. The owner publishes the menu as text, adds photos of the ube croissant to the Business Profile and asks regulars who love it to mention it by name. Over time, reviews and the menu tell Maps exactly what the cafe is known for.

sections.heading: Questions owners ask us
sections.body_html: Owners often ask whether they can ask customers to mention specific dishes in reviews. You can ask for honest reviews and suggest they mention what they ordered, but never offer rewards for reviews or write them yourself; Google's policies prohibit fake engagement. Another question is whether Google will publish a list for Orange County. Google hasn't said, so focus on the signals you control. Owners also ask how menus help on Maps. Text menus and dish photos make it easier for Maps and AI assistants to match your restaurant to searches for specific dishes.

sections.heading: Your own trend check
sections.body_html: You don't need Google's list to see your own trends. Read your last 50 reviews and note which dishes come up most, check which menu items sell best by month and look at the search terms in your Business Profile performance report. Together, these show what you're becoming known for. Feature those items in photos, posts and your website, and train staff to mention them to first-time guests.

sections.heading: Why reviews are discovery signals
sections.body_html: Google built the list partly from what people write in Maps reviews. When reviewers mention specific dishes, those words describe your restaurant in a way your own marketing can't. They help Google, and AI assistants that draw on reviews, connect your business to searches for that dish. A restaurant with hundreds of reviews that only say good food is harder to match to a specific craving than one whose reviews mention the house-made tortillas, the matcha tiramisu or the late-night menu.

sections.heading: Orange County's own food scene
sections.body_html: Orange County has its own strong food traditions, from Vietnamese restaurants in Little Saigon to Korean barbecue, taquerias, boba shops and cafes near Anaheim's attractions. Whatever your cuisine, the same approach works: make your signature dishes easy to find in your menu, photos and reviews. When a visitor in Anaheim asks Google Maps or an AI assistant for the best pho or the best boba nearby, those details decide who appears.

sections.heading: Questions to ask your team
sections.body_html:
• Which three dishes do customers mention most in reviews?
  • Is our menu published as text on our website and Business Profile?
  • Do we have recent photos of our signature dishes on Maps?
  • Do we reply to reviews and thank people for mentioning specific dishes?
  • Are seasonal items listed while they're available and removed when they're not?
  • Do our hours, including late nights, match on every listing?

Fixing even two or three of these makes it easier for diners, Google Maps and AI assistants to understand what your restaurant is known for, which is the real lesson behind Google's list.

sections.heading: The short version
sections.body_html: Google's Fan-Favorite Dining List shows Maps finds trends in what diners write and where they go. Anaheim and Orange County restaurants should publish menus as text, show signature dishes and encourage specific reviews.
